chapter: Cyber Security, Cyber Crime and IT Law
questionText: What does Section 43A of the Indian IT Act mandate for corporate bodies possessing Sensitive Personal Data (SPDI)?

options.text: Implementing reasonable security practices and procedures; failing which the corporate body is liable to pay compensation to affected victims
Maintaining an immutable audit log of all user transactions for a minimum of ten years to prevent data tampering
Disclosing the encryption keys to all stakeholders before storing any personally identifiable information in the database
Reporting every individual data entry event to the Centre for Cyber Security within 24 hours for real-time monitoring

detailedSolution: Section 43A of the Information Technology Act, 2000 mandates that any body corporate responsible for collection, handling, or storing sensitive personal data or information must follow such reasonable security practices and procedures as may be specified under the Act. If a body corporate fails to follow these practices and suffers a security lapse resulting in wrongful loss or wrongful gain to a person, the body corporate shall be liable to pay damages (compensation) to the person so affected. Option A correctly describes this civil liability and security mandate. The other options describe specific technical or procedural requirements (such as long-term audit logs, key disclosure, or real-time reporting) that are not the primary legal mandate of Section 43A, which focuses on the standard of care (reasonable security) and the consequence of negligence (compensation).

solution.quick: Correct answer is Implementing reasonable security practices and procedures; failing which the corporate body is liable to pay compensation to affected victims.
solution.concept:
Section 43A holds corporations civilly liable for financial damages if negligence in security protocols leads to unauthorized data breaches.
Hence, Option A is correct.
solution.detailed:
Section 43A holds corporations civilly liable for financial damages if negligence in security protocols leads to unauthorized data breaches.
Hence, Option A is correct.
